overview.text: Today's key developments span market shifts, hardware design breakthroughs, regulatory scrutiny, and foundational research challenges. The Nasdaq erased gains amid an AI sell-off impacting Anthropic's second day, while regulatory pressures intensified as the US SEC launched a probe into Nvidia examining potential accounting issues. In hardware innovation, researchers discovered, designed, and verified a new CPU architecture completely by AI named Frostbite. Labor activism also emerged as Google workers urged their employer not to punish schools rejecting AI tools. Within research and releases, new studies audited success checkers in simulated manipulation benchmarks and examined diverse sampling limitations in language models, alongside trending multimodal model releases such as thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini, RadixArk/DaisyRose-27B, and Cloudflare/clairic. Additionally, human-led mathematical analyses contrasted with AI-assisted claims regarding proofs for the Riemann Hypothesis, offering diverse perspectives for technical practitioners navigating the current ecosystem.

entries.title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
entries.summary: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task.
entries.why: Audits the reliability of success checkers in simulated manipulation benchmarks for researchers.

entries.title: A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models
entries.summary: Language models often produce high-quality individual samples but poor sets, with repeated samples clustering around the same semantic modes.
entries.why: Analyzes how language models struggle with diverse set sampling despite high individual quality.

entries.why: Integrates structured EHR data and clinical notes for improved diabetic readmission prediction.

entries.title: Advancing Science Together: Highlights From the Open Source AI For Science Summit
entries.summary: We brought researchers from universities, hospitals, and industry together for the Open Source AI for Science Summit, an event built around using open source AI to accelerate scientific discovery.
entries.why: Explores community efforts to accelerate scientific discovery using open source AI frameworks.

entries.title: Quoting Ravi Vakil
entries.summary: Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of [Generalized Riemann Hypothesis], and Brian Conrad has been looking closely at it for months and gave extensive feedback which is being incorporated, and it is so far looking good. It is all human, with no AI.
entries.why: Highlights a human mathematical proof process without AI assistance.

entries.title: Quoting Levent Alpöge
entries.summary: I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too.
entries.why: Discusses a claimed mathematical proof for the Riemann Hypothesis developed with Claude.
